comment: One row per (GCC 16.x version, platform). `available: false` cells are planned but skipped -- this is the same mechanism used for GCC 16.3.0 before it is released. Enabling a cell is a one-line edit: flip `available` and fill `artifacts` with a URL + sha256 for each pinned file. Never point a cell at a moving tag.

full_build.comment: Gate mode (the fast compiler capability probe) runs on every push and PR. Full engine configure + build runs on these events, or when workflow_dispatch asks for mode=full. A cell may set `full_build: false` when a known capability gap would make CMake stop at configure time; `full_build_reason` must then say why. `expected_probe_failures` lists probes that are known to fail for that compiler -- the gate reports them as annotations instead of failing the job, and warns if one unexpectedly starts passing. Neither field hides a NEW failure.

cells.label: GCC 16.1.1 / Linux
cells.note: There is no upstream gcc-16.1.1.tar.xz: 16.1.1 is the version the GCC 16.1 branch carried between the 16.1.0 (2026-04-30) and 16.2.0 (2026-08-07) releases. Fedora 44 GA and Arch shipped it as a dated snapshot; Arch keeps exactly that snapshot in its immutable archive. Three packages from the SAME build (r12+g301eb08fa2c5-1) are pinned: the compiler, libgcc and libstdc++. They need glibc >= 2.38, so ubuntu-24.04 (2.39) is the oldest usable runner; ubuntu-22.04 (2.35) is not.
cells.full_build_reason: Verified against the pinned snapshot: with -freflection, GCC 16.1.1 rejects Jolt's incomplete static data member (`union { T mElements[N]; ... }` instantiated while Vec3 is incomplete). cmake/ToolchainCapabilities.cmake makes that probe FATAL at configure time, so a full engine build cannot start. Released GCC 16.2.0 passes it. The gate still runs every other probe on 16.1.1 and reports the gap as a warning.

cells.label: GCC 16.1.1 / MSYS2 UCRT64
cells.unavailable_reason: No UCRT64 toolchain reports 16.1.1. WinLibs publishes 16.1.0 and 16.2.0 UCRT builds, and MSYS2's UCRT64 archive has mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-gcc 16.1.0-1..7 and 16.2.0-3..6 -- no 16.1.1. Substituting 16.1.0 would silently test a different compiler, so this cell stays skipped until a literal 16.1.1 UCRT64 artifact is published. See .github/gcc16/README.md for the 16.1.0 UCRT pin if a 16.1.x lane is wanted instead.

cells.label: GCC 16.2.0 / Linux
cells.note: The exact six conda-forge artifacts scripts/install-gcc-prebuilt.sh already pins for the jammy release lane. That script owns the download, checksum verification and the --sysroot=/ wrappers; the pins below are cross-checked against its ARTIFACTS block by `gcc16_matrix.py verify` so the two cannot drift.

cells.label: GCC 16.2.0 / MSYS2 UCRT64
cells.note: WinLibs' UCRT64 MinGW-w64 build of released GCC 16.2.0 (posix threads, SEH, mingw-w64 14.0.0 r3). The checksum is the one published in the release's .sha256 sidecar. It is a single self-contained archive, so no pacman compiler package is installed: MSYS2 supplies the shell, cmake, ninja and unzip, while this archive supplies the compiler. The DLLs in its bin/ must be on PATH (see cmake/HostToolRuntime.cmake).

cells.label: GCC 16.3.0 / Linux
cells.unavailable_reason: GCC 16.3 is not released yet (no gcc-16.3.0 tarball, no conda-forge gcc_impl_linux-64 16.3.0). When it is: add the six pinned .conda artifacts with their sha256, add that version to scripts/install-gcc-prebuilt.sh, and flip `available` to true. Until then this cell is skipped rather than failing the workflow.

cells.label: GCC 16.3.0 / MSYS2 UCRT64
cells.unavailable_reason: GCC 16.3 is not released yet, so neither WinLibs nor MSYS2 UCRT64 publishes a 16.3.0 toolchain. When one does: pin its archive URL + sha256 and flip `available` to true. Until then this cell is skipped.
